transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

Well… mostly sleep, I suppose. I don’t want to overstate it, but it’s gotten pretty out of hand. For a while I was waking after just two or three hours and feeling like I could get up and start drafting plans, like I was ready to go.

Now it’s less useful than that. I’m lying awake before dawn with my stomach all tight, and I don’t really feel rested. It’s just become… unmoored, if that makes sense.
During that time when you were sleeping only two or three hours, did you feel unusually high or unusually irritable?

Yes… I suppose I did. I mean, at first I would’ve called it a good mood, maybe even a very good one. For a few weeks I felt almost brilliantly optimistic, like every problem had an obvious solution and obstacles were… well, trivial.

But I should be honest—if someone questioned me, I could get sharp. I’d snap, more than I’m proud of. It felt at the time like they were getting in the way, or trying to undermine me, when of course that probably wasn’t fair. Does that make sense?
During that period, did you have beliefs that other people said were not true or unrealistic?

I… yes, I think that’s fair to say. At the time it didn’t feel unrealistic, of course. It felt more like I’d finally seen everything clearly.

I truly believed I could fix my retirement accounts, advise several start-ups, and turn the arts council into a real regional powerhouse. And I suppose I thought my judgment was just… better than everyone else’s for a while. Saying it now, it sounds rather grandiose, doesn’t it? But I really did believe it then.
At that time, were you completely certain those beliefs were true, even when other people clearly told you they were not?

Yes… at the time, I was quite certain. I don’t love admitting that, because it sounds arrogant, but I really did believe I could repair my retirement accounts, advise three start-ups, and make the arts council into something much larger—regional, even.

And when people pushed back, I didn’t really take it in. I thought they just weren’t seeing what I was seeing, as if my judgment had suddenly become… superior, I suppose. That’s not a very flattering way to put it, but it was how it felt then.
During that time, did you hear or see things that other people could not?

No… I don’t think so. Not in the sense of hearing voices or seeing things that weren’t there.

I mean, I was very keyed up and probably reading too much into things, but I don’t remember actually hearing or seeing anything other people couldn’t. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
During that period, were you hospitalized because of your mood or behavior?

I… I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I don’t think I should say anything definite if I can’t remember it clearly.

There were people concerned about me, certainly, but whether it rose to being hospitalized because of my mood or behavior… I’d rather not overstate it. Is it all right if I say I’m not certain?
During that period, did your mood or behavior cause serious problems in your work, finances, or relationships?

Yes… I suppose it did. I’d like to say I was just “overcommitted,” but that probably isn’t quite honest.

My wife had to step in and take over the finances, and she stayed close to me because she was worried about my safety. And I stopped being reliable with the museum, the arts council, even friends… not showing up when I should have, or not following through.

It’s embarrassing to say, but yes, it caused real problems.
